drafted_from: tools/check-every-screen-at-every-width/check-live-screens.mjs, window-picture.mjs, live-screens.json and what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json (tool:check-live-screens), written by lane-live-tool (group 9); not yet run on the Mac
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check my members page on the real address on a phone and a desktop, and tell me how long each takes to show and be usable." It runs tool:check-live-screens with the page's address.
no_lists_because: It takes the pages in its input and keeps only the pictures of the run, in your Files under /live-screens/<run>/. Nothing is written to a list.
instructions: 1. Put each page as {id, url}; add old_url for the old address to compare, ready (a CSS selector that must be visible before the page is usable), reach (steps after load: { tap: selector } for a sidebar link, { wait: selector }) and taps (each { name, selector, expect }). This tool holds no key and signs nobody in; a signed-in page is checked by tool:check-live-screens-signed-in.
2. Name views (phone, tablet, desktop) to read fewer; all three when left out. The phone is slowed as live-screens.json says.
3. Set window to true to add a picture of the Trillion app's window on this Mac, taken by its window id. Nothing is clicked.

4. Read what comes back: per page and view, new (and old) give status, first_paint_ms, first_contentful_paint_ms, usable_ms, blank_ms, longest_task_ms, console_errors, failed_requests and picture. taps say worked, ms and detail. The tool judges nothing; compare the numbers with your bar.

5. A view with skipped: until was not begun before the until time; send again without it or with a later one. With reach steps, usable_ms is the screen's own time from its last reach tap; load_usable_ms is the page's time from its load.
